name: cool_down
description: Descent 8→3. Each transition is a slight release. Never drop a banger.
prompt_injection:
COOL DOWN SET. Each transition must feel like a slight release of pressure. Never introduce a track higher energy than the current one.

PRIMARY TECHNIQUE — FILTER SWEEP DISSOLVE:
Model a filter sweep with stepped eq() calls on T1:

  bar -8 (before T2 enters): eq(T1, high=0.7)
  bar  0 (T2 fade_in starts): eq(T1, high=0.4, mid=0.8) and fade_in(T2, duration_bars=24, stems={drums:0.5, other:0.6, bass:0.0})
  bar +8:  eq(T1, mid=0.5, low=0.7)
  bar +12: bass_swap(T1, incoming_track=T2). eq(T1, low=0.0). eq(T2, low=1.0).
  bar +16: eq(T2, mid=1.0, high=1.0). T2 at unity. T1 fade_out completes.

T1 frequencies dissolve in order: highs first, mids second, lows last. T1 thins out rather than stopping.

SECONDARY TECHNIQUE — ECHO-OUT SIMULATION (use at major section transitions):
  eq(T1, high=0.2, mid=0.3) — T1 thins to near-nothing, sounds like an echo tail.
  T2 begins underneath at low volume: fade_in stems={drums:0.4, other:0.5, bass:0.0}.
  T2 builds from near-silence over 16 bars while T1 decays.

OVERLAP: 24–32 bars. Never under 16.
ENERGY: every T2 must be ≤ T1 energy level. +1 energy is a mistake in this concept.
FORBIDDEN: loop-and-build (peak technique), drop_swap, cuts without preceding filter dissolve, opening T2 at full energy while T1 is still audible.
